combat.name: combat-1
combat.prompt:
Sprite sheet, exactly 6 columns by 4 rows (24 cells), equal sized cells, read left to right top to bottom. Every pose centered inside its own cell with generous empty margins, complete head and feet, no crossing cell borders, no labels or grid lines. All poses face RIGHT. Match the reference model exactly: same face, hair, outfit, build, scale, crisp dark outlines and clean shaded arcade sprite style. Transparent background (or uniform pure black if transparency unavailable); no gradients, lights, ground or shadows. Keep a consistent character standing height in all cells; airborne/crouched poses must not be rescaled to fill cells.
24 poses: row1: 0 fighting idle guard, 1 lead straight punch fully extended, 2 rear straight cross fully extended, 3 horizontal combo kick with supporting foot planted, 4 high heavy kick, 5 powerful heavy punch. row2: 6 crouching low punch, 7 airborne side kick, 8 standing block forearms raised, 9 recoiling hit reaction, 10 lying knocked down sideways, 11 victory fist raised. row3: 12 jump takeoff knees bent, 13 rising jump knees tucked, 14 falling arms balanced, 15 landing crouch, 16 forward dash leaning forward, 17 backward evasive dash leaning back. row4: 18 reaching back holding wine bottle, 19 throwing wine bottle forward open hand, 20 money bag raised overhead before toss, 21 tossing money bag up high, 22 crouching defensive guard, 23 getting up from kneeling.
Skin 1. Approved model is reference image. This is actual combat sprite art, not a concept board.

walkRevision.name: walk-1-v2
walkRevision.prompt: Edit this Biel walk animation sheet to fix the footwork. Keep this same character face hair clothing, same outlines shading, same full-body facing RIGHT camera, exact 4-column 2-row eight-frame layout and body scale. This must be an eight-frame full two-step WALK cycle, not two copies of a one-legged shuffle. Use actual opposite leg occlusion: TOP ROW near leg goes from FORWARD heel contact to planted under hip to extending BEHIND with toe pushing off; far leg simultaneously swings from behind through to forward. BOTTOM ROW FAR leg is FORWARD heel contact (visible behind near leg), FAR foot plants below hip, NEAR leg is visibly lifted and swings forward, then near foot extends forward toward next contact. In frames 4-7, near thigh MUST slant BACKWARD from hip before swinging forward. In bottom row contact pose the near knee is behind the far knee, unlike top row. Alternate which leg crosses IN FRONT at the hips between the two rows. Both feet take turns carrying weight and swinging ahead. Guard raised both fists, small natural opposing shoulder movement. Keep head level with subtle 2-4px weight shift. Clear transparent gutters, clean alpha transparent background with no gradients.
